children: (a) where-a-boat-carries-its-owner — settle the ADDRESS the owner is read from. The ticket file is the obvious candidate because boat_id already IS the ticket id, but the ticket's existing `owner` field is prose about components in the wrong namespace, so this is a real design question and not a lookup. GATING: nothing can be read until there is somewhere to read it from, so this proves before the parent.

questions.a: One assumption was load-bearing and is now named: THAT THE AUTHORITY REFUSAL WAS DOING WORK. It is not. cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py:1 compares `actor != boat_owner` and both values arrive from the SAME caller in the SAME call, so any caller can make them equal — including a caller with no standing at all. Measured 2026-08-10 during the first live fire of clear(): the very first production call refused as Unauthorized because the settlement had put boat_owner in the component namespace ('base'), and the fix that made it pass was to type a different string. A check a caller can satisfy by choosing its arguments is a declaration, not a refusal. Second assumption, examined and DISCHARGED: that the grant path rescues it — it does not, because Grant.authorizes() checks `by_owner == owner` where `owner` is again the caller-supplied boat_owner, so a caller who can state boat_owner can mint itself a grant from that same fictional owner.

One point I would have asserted wrapped and is not: WHERE the boat's owner is read FROM. The boat is the ticket (boat_id is the ticket id on every gated crossing), so the ticket file is the obvious address — but the ticket's existing `owner` field is PROSE about which COMPONENT owns which rung ('harbor_master owns the AUTHORITY rung; base owns THE DOOR'), which is exactly the namespace confusion this ticket exists to fix, one layer up. So the field cannot simply be read; either it gains a machine-readable sibling naming a MOVER, or the boat's owner lives somewhere else. That is a real open question and it is child (a) rather than smuggled past. Everything else is wrapped: the defect is measured, the mechanism is one comparison at one address, and the corrected settlement is already written beside it.

No exclusive-and-terminal collision; the congruency lab was recompiled and consulted 2026-08-10 before this cast, and boat_owner appears in exactly one intention — cairn/devices/harbor_master's own charter, which is this node's PARENT, not its rival. Two distinctions to record. (1) tickets/emit-refuses-an-uncleared-crossing (in flight, at WATCHME) landed the sixth seat and produced this finding on its first live fire; the whys are sequenced, not opposed: that ticket makes clearance MANDATORY at the door, this one makes the authority half of clearance MEAN something. Neither blocks the other — a mandatory gate whose Law 6 half is a declaration is still binding proven-space, resources and legality, which is three of its four refusals. (2) tickets/clearance-leaves-a-trace (cast 2026-07-26, at BUILDME) wants refusals recorded; that is about the gate's bookkeeping, this is about one refusal's content. Sequenced again, and in the useful direction: a trace would make this ticket's own horizon countable.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(boat-owner-comes-from-the-boat) -> [PROVED]

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact written against THIS ticket's falsifier, carrying the crossing census with each crossing's stated and resolved owner side by side, and the address the resolution read from.
watchme.consumer: harbor_master, the owner of the authority rung and the only component that can act on a finding that its own refusal is vacuous. Law 6: the back-edge that re-opens this node is the owner's act, never the probe's.
watchme.enough: when at least one crossing has been made by an actor that is NOT the box's single hand and the gate resolved that boat's owner from the boat — the horizon condition, discharged by evidence rather than by time. Explicitly NOT satisfiable by volume of CC-made crossings: a thousand crossings by one hand cannot distinguish a working owner-read from a constant.
watchme.nexus: hypothesize — 'did reading the owner from the boat actually make the Law 6 refusal bind?' is a claim about an outcome, and the hypothesize tree is where this system's kills and confirmations already accumulate.
watchme.trigger: fires on any pulse reaching harbor_master's address, reading the crossing census from the component histories under cairn/ from an era floor set at arming time. It reports a finding on either of two conditions: (a) a cleared crossing landed whose boat_owner is not the value the boat itself carries — the read having been bypassed or drifted, which is the sharpest signal and needs no sample; (b) every cleared crossing since the era floor resolves to the SAME owner string, which is falsifier clause (3): the check vacuous by a longer route, indistinguishable from health without counting. Each finding carries the offending crossings verbatim with their component, seq, actor and resolved owner, so the consumer never re-derives them.

filed_edges: [CORPUS] A CHECK WHOSE BOTH SIDES COME FROM ONE CALLER IS A DECLARATION. This is worth a corpus-wide sweep and not only a fix here: the same shape is what makes a self-declared cleared_by dangerous (the parent ticket's falsifier clause (3)), what killed auto-inherit for chart claims (a door-minted value can never disagree with the door), and what the two-witness rule keeps re-deriving in different words. Somebody should count how many gates in this system compare two values that arrived together.

intentions-congruency-lab/cairn-harbor_m.why: the lab is DERIVED, never authored: every file in it is named for the address of the charter it copies, so when harbor_master dropped into devices/ the compiler wrote a new file and the old name stopped being generated.
